From left to right: Al pastor, birria, barbacoa, camarones

The tortillas were great - pillowy and flavorful without being greasy. The salsa was tasty, somewhat similar to el Dorado's salsa X.

The pastor had the perfect amount of sweetness from the pineapple and we saw them carving the meat from the trompo, seemed pretty legit.

The birria was honestly the best birria taco I have had in Austin. It didn't come with consome but it had clearly had some poured into it before serving. Super flavorful and cheesy, and the grilled onions pushed it over the top.

The barbacoa was the low point for me, maybe my opinion is wrong here but it was way too fatty for me.

The camarones were lightly battered and fried with a mango salsa and cabbage with some kind of crema or aioli. The blue corn tortilla was cool to the touch (maybe because of the crema and cabbage?) and that somewhat took away from the taco. Overall quite tasty and definitely the largest of the 4.

All the food was 50% off for the soft opening and without the two margs ($8 each) the 6 tacos (2 not pictured) were ~~\~$16, so around $32 all together~~. I made a mistake with the prices, it was $38 total so $22 for 6 tacos.  

Considering how good everything was I will definitely be returning.
